name: Denman–Beavers matrix square root iteration
definition: For Hermitian positive definite A, set Y₀=A, Z₀=I and simultaneously update Y_(k+1)=(Y_k+Z_k^(-1))/2, Z_(k+1)=(Z_k+Y_k^(-1))/2; return Y≈A^(1/2), Z≈A^(−1/2).
variables: A input matrix; Y,Z coupled iterates; I identity
assumptions: Finite Hermitian positive definite matrix; accurate linear solves; exact arithmetic for the convergence proof; no extension to singular or indefinite inputs claimed
limitations: Two dense inverse actions per iteration; ill-conditioned inputs and finite precision may impair accuracy; small product residual alone does not establish the correct square-root branch
failure_conditions: Unresolved inverse solve or nonfinite iterate
Residual, symmetry or positive definiteness requirement not met
computation: Use simultaneous updates from the old pair via linear solves with identity right sides. Require an accuracy policy for Y²−A, ZY−I and Hermitian positive definiteness, monitor update size and stop on unresolved accuracy or iteration budget.

source.citation: Higham, N. J. (2006), Computing Matrix Functions by Iteration, University of Manchester, slide 19, https://www.maths.manchester.ac.uk/~higham/talks/lille06.pdf ; Higham (2020), What Is the Matrix Sign Function?, https://nhigham.com/2020/12/15/what-is-the-matrix-sign-function/ (block relation); positive-definite specialization independently derived.

application: General numerical computation of a positive definite square root and its inverse.
required_inputs: Hermitian positive definite matrix, solve precision, residual and iteration policy
mechanism_note: Induction gives Y_k=AZ_k and both iterates are positive definite functions of A. For eigenvalue a>0, y_next=(y+a/y)/2 and y_next−√a=(y−√a)²/(2y), yielding positive iterates, monotone convergence after the first step and quadratic local convergence. Z follows by Z=A^(-1)Y. Applying Newton sign iteration to [[0,A],[I,0]] produces exactly the two coupled blocks; retain this useful structured variant, not a separate distinct algorithm. Cholesky factors generally do not square to A.

name: Newton iteration for a matrix polar factor
definition: For nonsingular square A, set X₀=A and X_(k+1)=(X_k+(X_k*)^(-1))/2; return U≈X_k and H≈U*A in the polar factorization A=UH.
variables: A nonsingular square matrix; X iterate; U unitary factor; H positive definite Hermitian factor; * conjugate transpose
assumptions: Finite real or complex nonsingular square matrix, accurate inverse actions; exact arithmetic for singular-value convergence; no rank-deficient or rectangular guarantee
limitations: Extreme singular values may slow initial progress; dense solves are costly; scaling and backward stability require separate analysis; near-unitarity alone is not a complete factorization certificate
failure_conditions: Singular input or unresolved inverse action
Nonfinite iterate or iteration budget exceeded
Orthogonality, reconstruction or positive-definiteness checks unresolved
computation: Solve X_k* W=I then average X_k and W. Monitor ||X_k*X_k−I||, relative update and reconstruction with H=X_k*A; check Hermitian structure and positive definiteness under the declared precision policy.

source.citation: Higham, N. J. (1986), Computing the Polar Decomposition—with Applications, SIAM J. Sci. Stat. Comput. 7(4), 1160–1174, https://eprints.maths.manchester.ac.uk/694/ (abstract); Higham (2020), What Is the Polar Decomposition?, https://nhigham.com/2020/07/28/what-is-the-polar-decomposition/ (formula and SVD relation).

application: General numerical computation of a square matrix polar factorization.
required_inputs: Nonsingular square matrix, inverse-action accuracy, iteration and factorization residual policy
incompatible_methods: Rank-deficient or rectangular input for this recurrence
mechanism_note: Write A=PΣQ* with all σ_i>0. The iterates preserve P,Q and update each positive singular value by σ_next=(σ+1/σ)/2, with σ_next−1=(σ−1)²/(2σ). Thus U=PQ* and H=QΣQ* in the limit, with local quadratic convergence. Newton sign iteration on [[0,A],[A*,0]] preserves the adjoint block structure and gives exactly this update. Count as a structured sign-iteration variant; it does not compute a least-squares solution.

name: Newton iteration for the matrix sign function
definition: For square A with no eigenvalues on the imaginary axis, set X₀=A and X_(k+1)=(X_k+X_k^(-1))/2; the target S=sign(A) acts as +I on the right-half-plane generalized eigenspace and −I on the left-half-plane generalized eigenspace.
variables: A input matrix; X iterate; S matrix sign; I identity
assumptions: Finite square matrix with spectrum disjoint from the imaginary axis; accurate inverse actions; exact arithmetic for the convergence proof
limitations: Potentially slow initial progress for extreme eigenvalue magnitudes; nonnormality and eigenvalues near the imaginary axis can amplify numerical error; ||X²−I|| alone cannot verify the chosen invariant subspaces
failure_conditions: Spectrum on the imaginary axis or unresolved spectral separation
Unresolved inverse solve or nonfinite iterate
Residual or invariant-subspace accuracy policy not satisfied
computation: Perform inverse actions via linear solves and average with the previous iterate. Monitor involution and commutation residuals and relative updates; require a justified accuracy policy for the intended spectral subspaces, not just an involution residual.

source.citation: Higham, N. J. (2020), What Is the Matrix Sign Function?, https://nhigham.com/2020/12/15/what-is-the-matrix-sign-function/ (definition, Newton recurrence and block identities); convergence argument independently derived.

application: General numerical spectral splitting and matrix-function evaluation.
required_inputs: Square matrix, spectral separation conditions, inverse-action precision and accuracy policy
mechanism_note: S commutes with A and S²=I. Define G_k=(X_k−S)(X_k+S)^(-1). Direct substitution using commutation gives G_(k+1)=G_k². Each eigenvalue of G₀ is (λ−s)/(λ+s), with s=+1 or −1 chosen by the half-plane, so its modulus is less than one. Hence G₀^(2^k)→0 even for finite Jordan blocks, and X_k=(I−G_k)^(-1)(I+G_k)S→S. The identity X_next−S=X_k^(-1)(X_k−S)²/2 gives quadratic local convergence. Distinct matrix-function recurrence, not the scalar Newton root solver or the matrix exponential.
